name: Uganda
sources: GDP $4.3bn and 17.5m people (World Bank, 1990). Output was still below the 1970 level after Amin, the 1979 war and the Luwero bush war.

Inflation 33.1% in 1990, down from a peak near 200% in 1987-88 that had required a currency reform with a 30% conversion tax; Bank of Uganda rediscount rate around 35%. Coffee was over 90% of exports and the International Coffee Agreement quota system collapsed in July 1989, halving the price.

Tax take 7% of GDP — the lowest in the shipped roster and not a typo. Uganda had almost no functioning revenue administration in 1990; the Uganda Revenue Authority was created in 1991 precisely because of this figure.
Defence 3.1% of GDP for an NRA of roughly 70,000, swollen by absorbing defeated formations, and running counter-insurgency in Acholiland at the same time.

Authoritarianism 0.72 and stability 40: Museveni's National Resistance Movement had held power since January 1986 under a no-party 'Movement' system in which parties existed but could not campaign. The National Resistance Council's term was extended by five years in October 1989 without an election; the first Movement-system national elections were 1996.

Separatism 0.30: the north. Alice Lakwena's Holy Spirit Movement was broken in 1987 and Joseph Kony's remnant became the Lord's Resistance Army in 1988; the West Nile front and Karamoja were also unpacified. A north-south split running back to the colonial recruitment pattern, not a border dispute.
Military strength 3: light infantry with captured stock, effective in the bush and with nothing else.
